title: SkillsFuture-equivalent Scheme for Singaporeans Aged under 25
what_it_is: SkillsFuture-equivalent Scheme for Singaporeans Aged under 25

sections.label: PSEA for approved programmes
sections.summary: Approved programmes exist at publicly-funded post-secondary institutions, and Singaporeans there can use PSEA balances for selected extra-curricular training or enrichment programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: First, there are approved programmes at certificate, diploma, post-diploma, undergraduate and postgraduate levels at our publicly-funded post-secondary education institutions (PSEIs).

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: In addition, Singaporeans who are studying in these PSEIs can also use their PSEA balances to pay for fees and charges on selected extra-curricular training or local and overseas enrichment programmes.

sections.label: PSEA and Opportunity Fund access
sections.summary: Singaporeans under 30 have access to avenues like PSEA and the Opportunity Fund, including around 2,000 WSQ courses, most listed in the SkillsFuture Credit course directory.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to thank Dr Tan for his supplementary question.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to assure Dr Tan and all the Members that Singaporeans under 30 have access to avenues like the PSEA I mentioned, or even when they are in the tertiary institutions, the Opportunity Fund, to help them pursue extra-curricular courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: If they are using PSEA balances to pursue the courses, it includes around 2,000 of the WSQ courses and the bulk of these WSQ courses are also listed in the SkillsFuture Credit course directory.

sections.label: SkillsFuture initiatives for young Singaporeans
sections.summary: SSG and WSG work with tertiary institutions on initiatives like enhanced internships, the SkillsFuture Young Talent Programme and the SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programme for young Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: While SkillsFuture Credit caters for Singaporeans 25 years old and above, our young Singaporeans have access to many learning opportunities via a wide spectrum of SkillsFuture initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG), Workforce Singapore (WSG) work very closely with our tertiary institutions to scope out initiatives like enhanced internships and even the SkillsFuture Young Talent Programme where young Singaporeans can be involved in overseas immersion programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: After graduation from polytechnics and ITEs, our young Singaporeans can then move on to the SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programme where they can study and work at the same time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: So, we want to assure the Member that SSG, WSG will continue to work very closely with our tertiary institutions to really help our young Singaporeans gain the relevant experience in training, whether in school or workplace, through the various SkillsFuture programmes.
